# API Contract Requirements Quality Checklist: SpamDetector API

**Purpose**: Validate that the HTTP API contract requirements for `POST /spam-check/email` are
complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation. This is a "unit test for the
requirements" — it evaluates how the contract is specified, NOT whether the endpoint works.
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [contracts/spam-check-endpoint.md](../contracts/spam-check-endpoint.md) · [contracts/openapi.yaml](../contracts/openapi.yaml)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Request Contract Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the HTTP method and path (`POST /spam-check/email`) specified unambiguously as the only endpoint? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the request body content type specified as raw text (not JSON), and is that requirement stated explicitly rather than implied? [Completeness, Contract §Request]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the accepted body content classes (plain text, HTML, MIME, headers, arbitrary formatting) enumerated in the requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the `x-openai-api-key` header documented as required, including the consequence of its absence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the `x-openai-model` header documented as optional, including its default and passthrough behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the non-empty and maximum-size (1 MB) constraints on the request body both specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]

## Response Contract Completeness

- [ ] CHK007 Are all four `ApiResult<SpamResult>` envelope fields (`result`, `httpCode`, `isError`, `errorMessage`) defined with types and nullability? [Completeness, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK008 Are all four `SpamResult` fields (`spam`, `confidence`, `promptInjectionDetected`, `reason`) defined with types and constraints? [Completeness, Spec §Structured output]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the success-response shape fully specified (result populated, httpCode 200, isError false, errorMessage null)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the error-response shape fully specified (result null, isError true, non-sensitive errorMessage, mapped httpCode)? [Completeness, Contract §Error responses]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the JSON field names (camelCase) specified so the serialized contract is unambiguous? [Completeness, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the set of possible response status codes (200/400/413/500/502) enumerated for the endpoint? [Completeness, Contract §Response]

## Contract Clarity & Measurability

- [ ] CHK013 Is the `confidence` field's numeric range (0–1 inclusive) stated as a testable constraint? [Clarity, Spec §Structured output]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the requirement that `httpCode` equals the actual HTTP response status stated as an objectively verifiable rule? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "empty body" defined precisely enough to be evaluated (e.g., zero-length vs. whitespace-only)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the model default trigger ("missing, empty, or whitespace") specified precisely rather than just "missing"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the strict-schema requirement (`additionalProperties: false`, all fields required) stated in a way a reviewer can verify against the JSON Schema artifact? [Measurability, contracts/spam-result.schema.json]

## Status-Code Mapping Consistency

- [ ] CHK018 Is each failure category mapped to exactly one status code without overlap or contradiction (400/413/502/500)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the mapping consistent across the spec, the endpoint contract doc, and the OpenAPI document? [Consistency, Contract + openapi.yaml]
- [ ] CHK020 Is "invalid model selection" consistently categorized (client 400 vs. upstream 502) across all requirement sources? [Conflict, Spec §FR-014, research.md §7]
- [ ] CHK021 Are the pre-provider rejection cases (missing key, empty body, oversized body) consistently defined as never reaching the provider? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]

## Error Payload Safety (Contract-Level)

- [ ] CHK022 Does the contract require that `errorMessage` never contains the API key, headers, stack traces, raw exceptions, or raw payloads? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK023 Are example error messages specified as non-sensitive category strings rather than raw failure detail? [Clarity, Contract §Error responses]
- [ ] CHK024 Is there a requirement that the API key is never serialized into any part of the response envelope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Constitution §II]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Are the eight acceptance scenarios each mapped to a specific expected status and envelope state in the contract? [Coverage, Spec §Acceptance scenarios]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the prompt-injection scenario's contract outcome defined (200 with preserved structure; `promptInjectionDetected` may be true; verdict not forced)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the oversized-body case given an explicit contract response (413, no provider call)? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the malformed/undeserializable provider output case given an explicit contract response (502, fail-safe, no repair)? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the default-model scenario (no/blank `x-openai-model`) given an explicit successful-contract outcome? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004]

## Documentation & Discoverability

- [ ] CHK030 Are the OpenAPI documentation requirements complete (method, path, required/optional headers, plain-text body, response model, status codes, BYOK behavior)? [Completeness, Spec §Documentation]
- [ ] CHK031 Is there a requirement that generated documentation contains no real/example API keys? [Completeness, Spec §Documentation]
- [ ] CHK032 Is BYOK behavior documented in the contract so callers understand the per-request key requirement and its non-persistence? [Clarity, Constitution §II]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
